reason: Verified per-site (RFC 0106 wave 4g): `scope.order_values.any?` (preloader/through_association.rb:33) — `Enumerable#any?` without a block on a Ruby Array, spelled `this.scope?.orderValues?.length > 0` (through-association.ts:82). A `.length` read emits no callee, so no TS call can credit the Ruby one (RFC 0092, JS_ENUMERABLE_ALIASES).

Verified per-site (RFC 0106 wave 4g): `owners.first.association(through_reflection.name).loaded?` (preloader/through_association.rb:20) is index-0 access on a Ruby Array, spelled `this.owners[0].association(...)` (through-association.ts:69). `Array#first` is a positional idiom with no JS call form (RFC 0092).

Deliberate: the source Preloader is handed a scope derived from `reflectionScope`/`preloadScope` rather than `scope`, because `throughScope` may already have eager-loaded the source (see the block comment at the call site).

through_association.rb:89 `.reduce(:merge)` takes a Symbol as its ONLY argument and answers nil for an empty collection. JS `Array#reduce` takes a function and THROWS on an empty array with no initial value, so the seed is what stands in for Ruby's nil answer. Language shortcoming.
